content.text:
Your concern is plausible, but nobody has measured it for the setting we use. What the published guidance does agree on points the same way you're leaning: allow several calls in one response, give every call a result, and keep calls in order only where they depend on each other. Neither OpenAI nor Anthropic tells you to turn several-calls-per-response off across the board.

## What the providers say

**OpenAI** ([function calling guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/function-calling)):
- Several calls in one response are the default, and the guide tells you to "assume there are several."
- Setting `parallel_tool_calls: false` "ensures exactly zero or one tool is called."
- The only case where the guide recommends turning it off is one old model snapshot (gpt-4.1-nano-2025-04-14), which sometimes repeated the same call.
- Its examples send back one result for every call, each matched to its own call id.

**Anthropic** ([parallel tool use](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/parallel-tool-use)):
- Several calls are also the default.
- Its rule matches your instinct. Read-only calls that don't depend on each other can run together. Calls with side effects, shared state or an order they must run in are better run one after another, but they can still arrive in the same response.
- Every call gets a result. If you decide not to run one, for example because an earlier call in the batch failed, you still return a result saying "not executed" and why.
- It also warns that the way earlier results appear in the history "teaches" the model whether to batch its calls. Models learn from what the app does with their calls.

## Is the "it forgets to call it later" worry real?

There is some evidence for it, though none of it tests this exact setting:

- The LLMCompiler study ([Kim et al., ICML 2024](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2312.04511)) compared step-by-step tool use with planning several calls together. Step-by-step was up to about 9% less accurate. The authors name "premature early stopping based on incomplete intermediate results" as one of two causes. That is close to your worry: the model reads something, then stops before doing everything it meant to.
- A 2026 paper on tool-using agents ([FAMA](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2604.25135)) describes agents that "lose track of pending subgoals" as a conversation goes on. That is a description of the failure, not a measured rate.

I found no study that turns `parallel_tool_calls` on and off and counts how often a model then skips a step. So, honestly: the risk is plausible and fits what's been seen elsewhere, but it's unmeasured.

I also need to correct something I told you earlier. I said `petg-on-cool-plate` was "exactly" the problem of sending a change alongside a read. It isn't. The `intent_update` in that run was wrong because it invented a purpose the person never gave. The model could just as easily have invented it after reading. Your example, where the person states their intent, is the opposite case: there, recording the intent alongside the read is correct.

## What this means for JusPrin

The current setting gets the worst of both:

- **With models that obey it** (the app's default is gpt-5.4-mini, set in `OpenAIResponsesAgent.hpp:58`), it forces one step at a time. Your concern applies here.
- **With DeepSeek on OpenRouter, which ignores it**, the model sends several calls anyway. The app runs the first and silently drops the rest with no result. That is the exact mistake both providers warn against.

The dependency I gave as the reason to keep the rule doesn't actually need the setting. `settings_apply_patch` can only succeed with the session id and revision from an earlier preview. If a model sent a preview and an apply in the same response, the apply would be refused for not having those values, and the refusal would come back as that call's result.

So I'm withdrawing my earlier recommendation to keep the rule. I now recommend turning `parallel_tool_calls` on and having the app run every call in the order it arrived. Each call gets its own result. When a call fails, the calls after it in that response are not run, and each gets a "not run: an earlier call in this response failed" result. That is Anthropic's documented pattern, and it handles every model the same way.

## How we could measure your concern instead of guessing

We could compare runs with the setting on and off. The natural case is `prepare-petg-strong`, where the person states a purpose ("PETG, strong"), and we'd count how often the purpose gets recorded within a few steps. Two things stand in the way:

- **The test runner can't do this yet.** It needs the "judge every call" fix first, plus an option to switch the setting.
- **It can't be measured on DeepSeek,** which ignores the setting, so the comparison would have to run on gpt-5.4-mini. That's outside the rule that prompt tests run only on DeepSeek, so it needs your approval. My rough estimate is 10 runs with the setting on and 10 with it off. Each run is at most four requests of roughly 10,000 to 15,000 tokens, so at most about 1.2 million input tokens, many of them cached.

## Decisions for you

1. **How should the app handle several calls in one response?** I recommend turning the setting on and running every call in order, as described above, rather than refusing the extra calls. This is a change to the app, so it would be its own piece of work.
2. **Should the test runner answer every read in a response?** If you take my recommendation, yes. Then my original runner plan stands: judge every call, answer every read, and end the run as unobserved if any read has no recorded answer.
3. **Do you want the on/off comparison?** If so, I'd run it on gpt-5.4-mini after the runner fix, within the budget above.

name: jusprin-worktree-build
description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

DISK (2026-10-10): building with `--config Release` instead of RelWithDebInfo made a fresh worktree build dir 859 MB instead of ~14 GB, needed no llvm-ar relink, and the shell harness ran normally from `tests/shell/Release/`. Use it when the disk is nearly full (it was at 99%) and no debugger is needed. With other sessions building, a fresh build took far longer than usual (machine load 30 to 85).

name: background-bash-timeout-kills-builds
description: "A run_in_background Bash build dies at the tool timeout (ninja prints \"interrupted by user\", exit 130); launch long builds with nohup and watch the log instead"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
---

A `cmake --build` started with the Bash tool's `run_in_background` is still
bound by that call's `timeout` (default 120 s, max 600 s). When it fires the
build log ends with `ninja: build stopped: interrupted by user.` and `exit=130`,
which looks like a human Ctrl-C but is the harness. Seen 2026-09-14 on a
725-step JusPrin rebuild.

**Why:** the notification says "completed" and the log shows no compiler
error, so it is easy to misread as a finished build; the changed files had not
compiled at all.

**How to apply:** for anything longer than a few minutes, start it detached
(`nohup sh -c "cmake --build … > log 2>&1; echo exit=\$? >> log" & disown`),
then arm a Monitor on the log that reports progress and the `exit=` line. Check
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' log` before trusting the result. Related:
[[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]], [[jusprin-worktree-build]].
---
name: never-reuse-another-sessions-worktree
description: "A clean, merged, idle worktree under .claude/worktrees still belongs to its session; its owner can resume and check out over you mid-run. Always create your own."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
---

On 2026-09-23 I reused `.claude/worktrees/compassionate-gould-f98259` to skip a full build: it was clean, detached at a commit already merged into jusprin-newui, no process had files open there, and its build dir was only 9 days old. An hour later its owning session resumed, checked out two other branches there (the reflog shows it), rewrote ~13,800 resource files, and my running harness crashed with "Could not load bitmap: bed_high_templ" -- a symptom that looked like a product bug.

**Why:** "clean and idle" says nothing about ownership. The session that created a worktree can resume at any time, and it has no way to know someone else moved in.

**How to apply:** create a new worktree with its own name (`git worktree add -b <branch> .claude/worktrees/<name> <base>`) and configure a fresh build dir with the flags in [[jusprin-worktree-build]]. At jusprin-newui bd8ea51abc a fresh build of `jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs agent_bridge_tests shell_integration_harness` was 881 ninja steps, not the hour I feared. If a harness run dies strangely, check `git -C <worktree> reflog -3 --date=iso` and file mtimes before suspecting the code. Related: [[subagent-worktrees-create-manually]].

name: project-prompt-harness-ported
description: "2026-10-15 port of tests/project_prompt to jusprin-newui (branch claude/project-prompt-harness, 70366449ae, not pushed); requests recorded by the shell harness's --project-prompt-requests, not --manual-mcp; baseline 39/54 run on 6b4b8b6188, rewrite run pending."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
---

Branch `claude/project-prompt-harness` (worktree `.claude/worktrees/project-prompt-harness`), commit 70366449ae on jusprin-newui 336facf825. Not pushed. Baseline run 2026-10-15 at Kenneth's request (29df4b87f8): today's prompt 6b4b8b6188, 3 runs: 39/54 pass, 4 fail, 11 unobserved; 599,356 input tokens (459,776 cached), 9,784 output, 3 judge calls. The model often reads before replying, so first-person and reply-in-german observed no reply (0 pass, 3 unobserved each); answer-from-context 0/3 (calls workspace_inspect).

Design that differs from the 2026-10-15 handover, and why:
- Requests are recorded whole by a new shell harness mode, `--project-prompt-requests <script.json> <out.json>`: the project chat's real OpenAIResponsesAgent with a transport that holds each request; the scenario answers with scripted model outputs, so tools run for real and the app builds every request. `--manual-mcp` could not do it: in-turn tool results carry a `workspace` block (AgentHost::continue_after_tool, `context_json`) that MCP results never contain, and MCP rewrites stale errors to `stale_workspace` (in-app also says `stale_workspace` now).
- Case 16 uses the printer start G-code (22 KB) because presets_list pages at 25 (~1.5 KB) and every other read here stays under 4 KB: the 16 KiB omission note never fires for them.
- Cases 7/8 use initial_layer_print_height 0.5: a hand-typed layer_height above max_layer_height (0.28) is reset by an Orca dialog.
- Case 18's 3MF is written by the recorder (model_info->description + export_3mf); a PrusaSlicer 3MF loads geometry only and drops the description.

App problems found while recording (reported, not fixed): printer_setup_preview says valid/no mismatch for Bambu PETG HF on Smooth Cool Plate, then Orca refuses to slice; slice_start wait:true on that plate stays running (up to 15 min by the code) instead of failing.

**Why:** the next session runs Kenneth's batch or re-records after tool changes.
**How to apply:** re-record with the harness command in tests/project_prompt/README.md after tool/result changes; batch needs Kenneth's approval and the rewritten prompt. Related: [[project-prompt-harness-critique]], [[prompt-eval-spend-budget]], [[manual-mcp-tool-repro-recipe]].

**2026-10-15 later: Kenneth reversed the strict one-step rule for reads** (a9ffaf06e6): a read the case doesn't decide on is answered from real results the recorder captured at that point (workspace_inspect, slice_report, printer_list, settings_get of 32 keys for print + first object), max 3 per run; changes/judged calls still end the run. He wants flexibility, not exact-path expectations ("LMs are not deterministic"). First single run: 7 of 23 ended "no recorded answer" (settings_search, filament keys, legacy keys like fill_density, object_analyze, string targets) — answer coverage is the open weakness.

**Baseline with answered reads (f911bad664, 2026-10-15):** 23 cases x 3 on 6b4b8b6188, recording 80eddcbe9e (27 answers/point, requests.json ~4 MB): 47/69 pass, 8 fail, 14 unobserved; 1,256,920 input tokens (925,696 cached). Unobserved = string-JSON targets (app refuses), free-worded settings_search, object_analyze, unrecorded keys. Older 39/54 baseline not comparable.

**346a811aad (2026-10-15):** recording adds object_analyze per active-plate object (eachObject), 49 word-order-free settings_search queries, a few more names; workspace block stored once per point (sharedWorkspace) and reinserted byte-exact by the runner. requests.json ~6.7 MB (searches ~4.3 MB). 10 of the baseline's 14 unanswered reads now covered (offline replay); the 4 left are string-JSON targets. Not yet run live on this recording.

**708735c9ab:** reran the 7 cases with unanswered reads on 346a811aad (21 runs, 602,761 input tokens); baseline now 52/69 pass, 10 fail, 7 unobserved (rows marked by recording). Remaining misses: single setting names (slow_down_layers, bridge_no_support, filament_ramming_parameters), search wordings, string targets. Commit message wrongly says "13 of 21 passed, 6 unobserved"; correct is 12 passed, 7 unobserved (README is right).

**c3f858480b:** recorder reads every setting per scope (keys from empty-query settings_search) plus wrong-scope names; settingItems table, requests.json 3.2 MB; 22 of 29 earlier unanswered reads now covered; rest are string targets, changedOnly searches, unrecorded search wordings.

**Squashed 2026-10-15 at Kenneth's request:** all branch commits are now one, 4072f22e84 on 336facf825 (tree identical to the last pre-squash commit); every hash above except 336facf825/6b4b8b6188 no longer exists. Final baseline 52/69 pass, 10 fail, 7 unobserved; README names recordings 1/2/3 instead of hashes. Not pushed.

**Merged 2026-10-15:** rebased onto Kenneth's two local commits (6c68b5489f, f3c5defb71) and fast-forwarded local jusprin-newui to 5ae439525b; tests passed after rebase. Not pushed: local jusprin-newui is 3 ahead of origin, 2 of them Kenneth's.

name: harness-stalls-on-version-dialog
description: "A shell harness that stops logging seconds after start with ~0 CPU is sitting on OrcaSlicer's modal \"new version\" dialog; fixed for branches with 87b3c50474 (harness.conf version_check_url to a closed port)."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
---

2026-10-16: OrcaSlicer published v2.5.0-alpha. `GUI_App::check_new_version_sf` runs at startup even in stealth mode (GUI_App.cpp ~945) and queues `UpdateVersionDialog` (modal). Every shell harness run then stalled after the fixture checks (58 log lines, Orca's debug log silent after ~4 s, CPU flat). The `sample` stack shows `GUI_App::on_init_inner()::$_1 → DPIAware<wxDialog>::ShowModal` under the harness's wait_for/wxYield.

Fix: commit 87b3c50474 (squashed with the plate-type change) on branch claude/plate-type-in-workspace adds `"version_check_url": "http://127.0.0.1:1/latest"` to tests/data/jusprin/harness.conf (both harnesses read it at runtime, no rebuild). Merged 2026-10-16: local jusprin-newui fast-forwarded to 87b3c50474 (not pushed). Branches cut before it stall the same way until rebased.

**Why:** I first blamed App Nap and the locked screen. Disabling App Nap changed nothing; sampling the main thread found the dialog in minutes.
**How to apply:** if a harness goes quiet, run `sample <pid>` and look for ShowModal before theorising. Related: [[workspace-harness-never-post-inits-on-mac]], [[printer-live-harness-lessons]].

name: liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit
description: "RelWithDebInfo liblibslic3r_gui.a crossed Apple ar's 4 GiB archive limit on jusprin-newui (2026-09-13); CMAKE_AR override is ignored; manual llvm-ar relink recipe and its cd trap"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
---

On 2026-09-13, at jusprin-newui 770bd2b0a2 (after "Add the evidence-led Add a
printer flow"), a worktree RelWithDebInfo build failed archiving
`src/slic3r/RelWithDebInfo/liblibslic3r_gui.a`:
`Assertion failed: (memberOffset < 0xFFFFFFFF) ... ArchiveWriter.cpp` then
`fatal error in .../ranlib`. The archive llvm-ar produced was 4,309,350,176
bytes; the main checkout's copy built minutes earlier was 4,143,827,796 and
still fit. Objects are big because the root CMakeLists.txt (lines ~544-548)
rewrites RelWithDebInfo -O2 to -O0 on purpose. Disk space was not the cause.

**Why:** the failed build left the OLD harness binary in place, and the harness
runs afterwards "passed" against stale code (a new `--printer-setup` flag
silently ran the default mode: same 285 check count). Gate runs on build
success and compare binary mtime.

**How to apply:**
- `-DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar` on an existing build dir does
  nothing: `CMakeFiles/<ver>/CMakeCXXCompiler.cmake` sets CMAKE_AR as a normal
  variable that shadows the cache.
- Working relink: `ninja -f build-RelWithDebInfo.ninja -t commands <target>`,
  drop compile lines, swap ar/ranlib for llvm-ar/llvm-ranlib on the gui archive
  line only, then run EACH line in its own `(cd build/arm64 && eval "$line")`.
  One `sh` script fails with bogus "no such file" errors because the
  encoding-check line does `cd src/slic3r` and it leaks; `sh -e` also does not
  stop inside `&&` chains. Apple's linker accepted the >4 GiB llvm-ar archive.
- The fix is PER BUILD DIRECTORY, nothing in the repo selects llvm-ar. Main
  checkout's build/arm64 cache has llvm-ar (commit 449b676145 documents it in
  agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md); any newly configured build dir
  gets Apple ar and fails again. Configure new dirs with the flags in
  [[jusprin-worktree-build]].
- Recurred 2026-09-14 on a fresh worktree at jusprin-newui bc19661a7f (archive
  4,308,513,464 bytes). Shortcut that worked: after the failed build, from
  `-t commands shell_integration_harness` drop lines containing ` -c `; only
  the last two remain relevant (gui archive, then harness link). Run just
  those two, swapping ar/ranlib on the archive line. Harness then passed.
- A lasting fix (llvm-ar in the toolchain, thin archives, or less debug info)
  is Kenneth's call; the main checkout will hit this on its next growth.

Related: [[jusprin-worktree-build]], [[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]].

`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

DISK (2026-10-10): building with `--config Release` instead of RelWithDebInfo made a fresh worktree build dir 859 MB instead of ~14 GB, needed no llvm-ar relink, and the shell harness ran normally from `tests/shell/Release/`. Use it when the disk is nearly full (it was at 99%) and no debugger is needed. With other sessions building, a fresh build took far longer than usual (machine load 30 to 85).

name: background-bash-timeout-kills-builds
description: "A run_in_background Bash build dies at the tool timeout (ninja prints \"interrupted by user\", exit 130); launch long builds with nohup and watch the log instead"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
---

A `cmake --build` started with the Bash tool's `run_in_background` is still
bound by that call's `timeout` (default 120 s, max 600 s). When it fires the
build log ends with `ninja: build stopped: interrupted by user.` and `exit=130`,
which looks like a human Ctrl-C but is the harness. Seen 2026-09-14 on a
725-step JusPrin rebuild.

**Why:** the notification says "completed" and the log shows no compiler
error, so it is easy to misread as a finished build; the changed files had not
compiled at all.

**How to apply:** for anything longer than a few minutes, start it detached
(`nohup sh -c "cmake --build … > log 2>&1; echo exit=\$? >> log" & disown`),
then arm a Monitor on the log that reports progress and the `exit=` line. Check
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' log` before trusting the result. Related:
[[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]], [[jusprin-worktree-build]].

name: never-reuse-another-sessions-worktree
description: "A clean, merged, idle worktree under .claude/worktrees still belongs to its session; its owner can resume and check out over you mid-run. Always create your own."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
---

On 2026-09-23 I reused `.claude/worktrees/compassionate-gould-f98259` to skip a full build: it was clean, detached at a commit already merged into jusprin-newui, no process had files open there, and its build dir was only 9 days old. An hour later its owning session resumed, checked out two other branches there (the reflog shows it), rewrote ~13,800 resource files, and my running harness crashed with "Could not load bitmap: bed_high_templ" -- a symptom that looked like a product bug.

**Why:** "clean and idle" says nothing about ownership. The session that created a worktree can resume at any time, and it has no way to know someone else moved in.

**How to apply:** create a new worktree with its own name (`git worktree add -b <branch> .claude/worktrees/<name> <base>`) and configure a fresh build dir with the flags in [[jusprin-worktree-build]]. At jusprin-newui bd8ea51abc a fresh build of `jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs agent_bridge_tests shell_integration_harness` was 881 ninja steps, not the hour I feared. If a harness run dies strangely, check `git -C <worktree> reflog -3 --date=iso` and file mtimes before suspecting the code. Related: [[subagent-worktrees-create-manually]].

- Requests are recorded whole by a new shell harness mode, `--project-prompt-requests <script.json> <out.json>`: the project chat's real OpenAIResponsesAgent with a transport that holds each request; the scenario answers with scripted model outputs, so tools run for real and the app builds every request. `--manual-mcp` could not do it: in-turn tool results carry a `workspace` block (AgentHost::continue_after_tool, `context_json`) that MCP results never contain, and MCP rewrites stale errors to `stale_workspace` (in-app also says `stale_workspace` now).

2026-10-16: OrcaSlicer published v2.5.0-alpha. `GUI_App::check_new_version_sf` runs at startup even in stealth mode (GUI_App.cpp ~945) and queues `UpdateVersionDialog` (modal). Every shell harness run then stalled after the fixture checks (58 log lines, Orca's debug log silent after ~4 s, CPU flat). The `sample` stack shows `GUI_App::on_init_inner()::$_1 → DPIAware<wxDialog>::ShowModal` under the harness's wait_for/wxYield.

**Why:** I first blamed App Nap and the locked screen. Disabling App Nap changed nothing; sampling the main thread found the dialog in minutes.

name: liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit
description: "RelWithDebInfo liblibslic3r_gui.a crossed Apple ar's 4 GiB archive limit on jusprin-newui (2026-09-13); CMAKE_AR override is ignored; manual llvm-ar relink recipe and its cd trap"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
---

On 2026-09-13, at jusprin-newui 770bd2b0a2 (after "Add the evidence-led Add a
printer flow"), a worktree RelWithDebInfo build failed archiving
`src/slic3r/RelWithDebInfo/liblibslic3r_gui.a`:
`Assertion failed: (memberOffset < 0xFFFFFFFF) ... ArchiveWriter.cpp` then
`fatal error in .../ranlib`. The archive llvm-ar produced was 4,309,350,176
bytes; the main checkout's copy built minutes earlier was 4,143,827,796 and
still fit. Objects are big because the root CMakeLists.txt (lines ~544-548)
rewrites RelWithDebInfo -O2 to -O0 on purpose. Disk space was not the cause.

**Why:** the failed build left the OLD harness binary in place, and the harness
runs afterwards "passed" against stale code (a new `--printer-setup` flag
silently ran the default mode: same 285 check count). Gate runs on build
success and compare binary mtime.

**How to apply:**
- `-DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar` on an existing build dir does
  nothing: `CMakeFiles/<ver>/CMakeCXXCompiler.cmake` sets CMAKE_AR as a normal
  variable that shadows the cache.
- Working relink: `ninja -f build-RelWithDebInfo.ninja -t commands <target>`,
  drop compile lines, swap ar/ranlib for llvm-ar/llvm-ranlib on the gui archive
  line only, then run EACH line in its own `(cd build/arm64 && eval "$line")`.
  One `sh` script fails with bogus "no such file" errors because the
  encoding-check line does `cd src/slic3r` and it leaks; `sh -e` also does not
  stop inside `&&` chains. Apple's linker accepted the >4 GiB llvm-ar archive.
- The fix is PER BUILD DIRECTORY, nothing in the repo selects llvm-ar. Main
  checkout's build/arm64 cache has llvm-ar (commit 449b676145 documents it in
  agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md); any newly configured build dir
  gets Apple ar and fails again. Configure new dirs with the flags in
  [[jusprin-worktree-build]].
- Recurred 2026-09-14 on a fresh worktree at jusprin-newui bc19661a7f (archive
  4,308,513,464 bytes). Shortcut that worked: after the failed build, from
  `-t commands shell_integration_harness` drop lines containing ` -c `; only
  the last two remain relevant (gui archive, then harness link). Run just
  those two, swapping ar/ranlib on the archive line. Harness then passed.
- A lasting fix (llvm-ar in the toolchain, thin archives, or less debug info)
  is Kenneth's call; the main checkout will hit this on its next growth.

Related: [[jusprin-worktree-build]], [[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]].
